overview: The Mega Food Park Scheme aims to link agricultural production to the market by bringing together farmers, processors, and retailers to maximize value addition, minimize wastage, increase farmers' income, and create employment opportunities, particularly in rural areas. It follows a 'Cluster' approach to create state-of-the-art support infrastructure in a defined agri/horticultural zone for setting up modern food processing units in industrial plots within the park, with an established supply chain. The scheme has been discontinued by the Government with effect from 01.04.2021, with provision for committed liabilities for ongoing projects only. As of the evidence, 25 Mega Food Parks are operational.
objectives: Link agricultural production to the market by bringing together farmers, processors, and retailers
Maximize value addition and minimize wastage
Create employment opportunities, particularly in rural sector
Create state-of-the-art support infrastructure in a well-defined agri/horticultural zone
Provide well-developed plots for entrepreneurs to set up food processing units
eligibility: The Mega Food Park project is implemented by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) which is a Body Corporate registered under the Companies Act. State Government, State Government entities and Cooperatives are not required to form a separate SPV for implementation of Mega Food Park project. Subject to fulfillment of the conditions of the Scheme Guidelines, the funds are released to the SPVs.
benefits: The scheme provides a mechanism to link agricultural production to the market, maximizes value addition, minimizes wastage, increases farmers' income, and creates employment opportunities, particularly in rural sector. It offers state-of-the-art support infrastructure including collection centers, primary processing centers, central processing centers, cold chain, and around 25-30 fully developed plots for entrepreneurs to set up food processing units with an established supply chain.
financial_support: Funds are released to the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) subject to fulfillment of the conditions of the Scheme Guidelines. The SPV is a Body Corporate registered under the Companies Act. State Government, State Government entities and Cooperatives are not required to form a separate SPV for implementation.
application_process: 1. Form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) as a Body Corporate registered under the Companies Act (State Government, State Government entities and Cooperatives are exempt from forming a separate SPV). 2. Ensure the SPV meets the conditions of the Scheme Guidelines. 3. Submit proposal for financial assistance. 4. Upon approval, funds are released to the SPV. 5. Develop the Mega Food Park with supply chain infrastructure including collection centers, primary processing centers, central processing centers, cold chain, and 25-30 fully developed plots for food processing units.
deadlines: The scheme has been discontinued by the Government with effect from 01.04.2021 with provision for committed liabilities for ongoing projects only.
